summary: Added write_chart_edits<W: std::io::Write + ?Sized> with complete pre-write validation, direct borrowed-chunk output, typed error sources, and six integration tests. All required checks pass.

Passed twice, including after clone-template bounds hardening.
Passed twice. First run: 165 existing tests and 5 new integration tests; final run: 165 existing tests and 6 new integration tests. No failures or ignored tests; zero doctests.

design_decisions: Both public edit paths use plan_chart_edits and validate_splices. Validation checks every range, preserves the original sorting key and error ordering, and checks all overlaps before any writer call. Shared splice_chunks yields the same ordered bytes to the buffered and streaming paths.

The writer is borrowed with W: io::Write + ?Sized, supporting trait objects. Unchanged chunks borrow the input XML and replacement chunks borrow planner-owned vectors. No complete input or output XML buffer is allocated to feed the streaming writer; existing structural-fragment allocation remains.

write_all provides short-write, Interrupted, and WriteZero behavior. A terminal I/O error immediately stops output and is retained intact, including custom payloads. The caller retains ownership and responsibility for flushing or closing the writer.

WritePatchError has Patch and Io variants and implements Debug, Display, and Error. Error::source returns the original typed error; PatchError receives an additive Error implementation. The new enum is non-exhaustive; all existing enum variants, struct fields, signatures, and exhaustive matching remain unchanged.
Public documentation distinguishes untouched output after validation failure from a possible written prefix after I/O failure. No rollback is promised once writing begins.

Clone-template access now uses checked ranges and checked subtraction before reading a fragment. Invalid template coordinates return existing patch errors instead of indexing or arithmetic panics. Redundant debug-only width assertions were removed because fresh fragment scanning supplies the actual coordinates.

Integration tests exercise every edit variant, ordering of same-anchor series insertions, combined value and structural edits, exact unchanged-byte preservation, trait-object writers, short writes and interruptions, late invalid/reversed/overlapping spans, invalid clone-template spans, preserved custom I/O payloads, and WriteZero. Existing inline tests were preserved.
Applied the supplied Rust style guidance within the explicit compatibility and file restrictions; did not alter fixed configuration, dependencies, or pre-existing API shapes.
limitations: Validation uses the existing edit planner and requires ChartData scanned from the same input XML; it does not establish provenance of arbitrary caller-constructed in-bounds coordinates.
Verification covers the isolated component and cached Rust 1.93.1 toolchain. No full document engine, upstream integration, or visual rendering validation was performed.
The no-complete-output-buffer property was verified through implementation structure, not allocation instrumentation or benchmark measurements.
No build, test, Clippy, or formatting failures occurred during this session.
